chapter_theme: The teacher finishes his account of the gods: the splendour of the heavens and their pleasures, the powers and spans of the four orders and the kalpa heavens up to thirty-three seas, and the highest gods under no lord; he notes that heaven's wealth, won by austerity, ends, and says that right vision with austerity keeps one from hell and brings endless bliss, as the king bows.

cast.role: the unnamed teacher who tells the king of the heavens and the orders of gods
King Payapati, who listens to the teaching

2047.reading: Those who stay true to their beloved, give up wine and flesh, give gifts and keep the home, together with the young women of their houses, are said to rise as gods among the highest, with light, the eight qualities and their pleasures.
2047.nuance: Line 3 ஓதினமுத்தேவராய் is read as 'the gods we have named'; the sense of முத்தேவர் here is not fixed, so the reading keeps only that these householders become gods.

claims.claim: a householder who gives, keeps from drink and flesh and is true to the spouse is born among the gods

2048.reading: The teacher says the gods in the sky above Mount Mandara show themselves like a rainbow, shining like images of fine gems while the heavenly ones hail them.

2049.reading: At that moment of birth as gods they are showered with flowers, bathed in nectar water, dressed in many ornaments, hailed and sung to, fanned with flower-gem whisks, and joined by women.
2049.event: A newly born god is showered with flowers, bathed in nectar and adorned while others hail him.

2050.reading: The gods' bodies shine without being dyed, their wreaths do not fade and their robes do not dull, and they bathe long in a great flood of delight.

2051.reading: The teacher says the gods who reach heaven have golden mansions, soft couches, gem hills and flying cars, and that there is nothing more to say of them than this.
2051.nuance: The 'nothing else to say' of line 4 turns the picture into an inventory: heaven is a list of comforts, and 2060 then says that even it has an end.

2052.reading: In the gods' assembly of musicians they watch a play, sit pleasantly with Indra while young women praise them, and live on jewelled upper terraces; this is all the sky holds for those who reach the gods' world.

2053.reading: With honey-voiced women to ravish the eye, a Mandara grove and drums sounding on a gem stage, the gods have such pleasures and their feats of power, and that is the report of them, the teacher says to the garlanded king.
2053.nuance: Line 4's செய்திறற்றொழில் is taken as the deeds the gods' power allows; the word is rare and the reading is not fixed.

2054.reading: When festivals are held for the Tirthankaras and light spreads over all directions, the peacock-like women and fruit-laden assemblies of the gods' own world are still not left behind by the gods.
2054.nuance: Line 1 தீர்த்தங்கள் திறந்தவர்க்கு and line 4 தம்முருவி னகலாரே are hard; the verse is read as the gods' worship of the Tirthankaras while they keep their own form, and the sense is not secure.

claims.claim: the gods honour the Tirthankaras at their festivals while remaining in their own forms and world

2055.reading: The gods have red eyes that never close, know neither night nor day, neither fire nor cold, and bear tall crowns heavy with strung gems.
2055.nuance: 'அமையாத பிறப்பறியார்' in line 2 is read as 'know no unfitting birth'; the phrase may mean something else.

2056.reading: The gods' powers are to shrink to an atom or swell very large, to arrive at a thought, to take whatever form they wish and many forms at will, and the like.
2056.nuance: Lines 3 and 4 are read as the remainder of the list of qualities; the construction is loose.

claims.claim: gods have powers of shrinking, growing, arriving at once and taking many forms

2057.reading: The teacher tells the king that heaven has levels and that the higher joy belongs to the higher beings; right vision, once perfected, is easy for the great, while others seldom get it.
2057.nuance: Line 4 can be read as saying the great find it easy or that it is mostly beyond the lesser; the reading keeps both halves.

claims.claim: right vision once perfected is easily gained by the great and rarely by others

2058.reading: The god's body shines as if rays of light had poured down on a gem image, and his gem crown and ruby bracelet burn with light of their own.
2058.nuance: Line 4's இனமுதலாச் சிடர்ந்தினிதி னியல்பாய் is corrupt-looking; only the shining is certain.

2059.reading: The wives of the divine kings have bodies of bright figurines and shining jewels, speak little, stay forever young and never wither.

2060.reading: Heaven's great wealth is all joy, with no pain even for a blink, and it comes through great austerity; but it ends some day, and those who understood the Lord's teaching saw that something higher lies above it.
2060.nuance: மிசை in line 4 may mean 'above' or 'further on'; the verse hints at release beyond heaven without naming it, and the following verses go on counting heaven's spans.

claims.claim: the great pleasure of heaven is won by austerity and has an end
a state higher than heaven exists

2061.reading: The Bhavana gods live a sea of years and a bit more, the equal gods here a palya, and the sun and moon gods similarly; after their span each one's destiny follows his own lot.
2061.nuance: Lines 1 and 2 are technical (கடல், பல்லம்) and the lines are read as the lifespans of the Bhavana, Vyantara and Jyotishka orders; the hit on exact figures is uncertain.

claims.claim: each order of gods has a fixed span measured in palya and sagara and then a destiny of its own

2062.reading: The lowest of the kalpa heavens are counted in pairs and groups, and their spans rise with each step up to twice eleven seas.
2062.nuance: The numbers of lines 1 to 3 are cryptic; the last line's twice eleven seas (twenty-two) fits the span of the highest of the kalpa heavens.

2063.reading: Above these come the three triples and the nine, each a step higher, and the span rises to thirty-three seas for the highest, the teacher says to the crowned king.
2063.nuance: The count of three, nine and fifteen doubled and three more reads as thirty-three; the arithmetic is the reading's own.

2064.reading: As for the divine kings of those realms, they are great beings who feel no longing for women and sit proudly in a lasting pleasure under their own radiance.
2064.nuance: Line 4 has a damaged word (சேயிடையொள் ெளாளிநிழற்ற); the sense of radiance is guessed.

claims.claim: the highest gods are free of desire for women and enjoy unbroken pleasure

2065.reading: The highest gods have bodies without flesh and limbs of light that spread over all the worlds, shining like crystal, with no one above them and none greater.
2065.nuance: Line 3's வெண்சங்கே ரிலைச்சையாம் is obscure; கோனிலா in line 4 is taken as 'having no king'.

claims.claim: the highest gods have no lord over them and none greater

2066.reading: Beyond that is a realm where equals live in a joy that never changes and no fall comes after long ages, the teacher says, a wide world where their kings sit enthroned.
2066.nuance: Line 1's அத்திதியா மதனிலமைந் தாலூணின் is hard; the reading keeps only an unchanging realm of equals.

2067.reading: The teacher closes by saying that the four destinies and the doors to them are as told, and that a person who stands in firm right vision and bears austerity avoids hell and the animal births and keeps a great, unfailing wealth.
2067.event: The teacher ends his account of the destinies and states the way to the unfailing wealth.

claims.claim: one who holds right vision and bears austerity escapes hell and animal births
such a one gains a great wealth that does not leave

2068.reading: When the king bows and asks for grace, the sage, the highest of those of great austerity, sets out how one reaches unending bliss, since a talk of welfare is not a place for flattery.
2068.nuance: Line 1 is read as the narrator's remark; it could also be the teacher's, and உறுதிகணன் is a doubtful word.
2068.event: King Payapati bows to the sage, who then lays out the way to endless bliss.

links.note: 2060 says heaven's pleasure comes by austerity yet ends, and that something is higher; Kural 346 says one who cuts off 'I' and 'mine' enters a world above the gods'.
links.teaches: The couplet's 'higher than the gods' is given a reason in the epic: the gods' world has a measured end, so only what lies above it can be a goal.

gains.a: The vague higher state is given a means, the cutting of ownership and the self, which the verse leaves unnamed.
gains.b: The couplet gains a ground for ranking the gods' world below renunciation: its joys are counted in years and end.

links.note: 2060 says heaven's wealth ends; Tirumanthiram 184 says time cuts down both the heaven-bound and the deed-bound.
links.teaches: Both deny that heaven is lasting, but the epic counts the ending in fixed spans of seas and tells of a state beyond, while Tirumular makes time's cutting a general law with no way out in that line.

gains.a: The ending of heaven gets a law of time that reaches everyone, in place of a bare statement of limit.
gains.b: The cutting down by time gets a scale, from a palya to thirty-three seas in 2061 to 2063, and a way above it by austerity.

links.note: 2051 itemises the gods' mansions, couches and cars as the whole of heaven; Kural 50 says the one who lives life as it ought to be lived will be counted among the gods.
links.teaches: What the couplet offers as the reward of right householding is shown by the epic as a list of comforts and then, in 2060, as a reward that has an end.

gains.a: The gods' world gets a stated goal in a householder's right life, which its inventory alone does not give.
gains.b: The couplet gains content for 'among the gods' and a limit on how far the reward goes.

links.note: 2052 lists the gods' play, Indra's company and jewelled terraces as heaven's whole stock; Naladiyar 137 asks whether heaven's city is sweeter than the gathering of learned men.
links.teaches: Naladiyar weighs heaven against the company of the learned and finds it no sweeter; the epic describes the gods' pleasures as only entertainment and ranks them below the teaching of 2067.

gains.a: The gods' amusements get a human measure by which they look modest.
gains.b: The comparison gains a full picture of what heaven's pleasures consist of, so the contrast is not left abstract.

links.note: 2065 says the highest gods have no lord over them and none greater; Tirumanthiram 266 says the ripened see the Lord's feet and the resolute rule his heaven.
links.teaches: The epic's top heaven stands under no ruling god, while Tirumular's heaven is the Lord's own; the conflict depends on reading கோனிலா as 'with no king above' and on taking 'his heaven' as lordship, not only as place.

gains.a: The claim of no lord over the highest gods meets a rival picture of a heaven that belongs to a Lord and is entered by grace.
gains.b: The Lord's heaven meets a counter-picture where beings of the highest rank answer to no one.

links.note: 2000 says gifts made by one who has grasped the true principles raise the giver among the best of the gods; 2047 names who these are: householders who give, avoid wine and flesh and stay true to the beloved.
links.teaches: 2047 widens the ground of 2000 from giving alone to abstinence and faithfulness, so the householder's whole conduct is what raises him.

links.note: 2057 says right vision is easy for the great and rare for others; 2067 says that standing in right vision with austerity keeps one from hell and animal births.
links.teaches: 2067 turns the rarity of right vision into a promise: who holds it with austerity escapes the lower births and keeps unfailing wealth.

links.note: 2060 hints at a state above heaven's ending joy; 2068 shows the sage, once the heavens are told, setting out how to reach endless bliss.
links.teaches: The hint of a state beyond heaven's end becomes, in the sage's closing, the thing the teaching moves toward: bliss that has no end.

source_issues: 2064 line 4 has a broken glyph (சேயிடையொள் ெளாளிநிழற்ற, vowel sign U+0BC6 after a space); the intended word is lost.
2062, 2063 and 2066 turn on technical lifespan words and cryptic numbers; they are marked uncertain.
The teacher is not named in these verses; as in chapter 88 he is inferred from the sarukkam's frame.
